title: GS20 4-round AES-128 / aes128-4r-mixture-integral-no-final-mc-precomputed-gs2020

target.description: 4 nonlinear AES-128 rounds without final MixColumns (source label 3.5 rounds). The attack recovers the full last-round key, permitting inversion of the AES-128 key schedule. Footnote 6 describes equivalent-key conversion when final MixColumns is present.

setting.key_relation: One unknown AES-128 master key; the public standard AES S-box is known, not the secret key.
setting.plaintext_model: Six nonadaptive plaintexts, three related pairs, reused for four anti-diagonal recovery passes.

time.note: Source Table 2 and Section 4.2 give the full four-pass online recovery cost. Published singleton lookup demonstrably discards valid candidates; this is not a verified completed-key-recovery budget.

data.note: Source Table 2 query count, reused across byte/anti-diagonal passes.

memory.note: Table 2 measures memory in 16-byte plaintext units: 2^28 such units, not 2^28 bytes.

preprocessing.note: Reusable public-S-box lookup table setup, separate from online time; not silently dropped from total cost.

success.description: The exact endpoint has no numerical complete-output success. The three-round distinguishing experiment95%/300000 cases and the approximate99.991% byte-distinctness figure are not whole-key recovery rates. The source writes one kappa to each table cell; the existing independently checked lost-valid-candidate conflict remains. The true zero-sum relation has probability1, but the printed singleton implementation is not assigned retention1. The C++ verification sentence has no trial-denominated recovery rate.

review.scope: Exact20-page proceedings edition; Sections4.1–4.2, Algorithms2–3 and Equations7–8. No probability was added: zero-sum1 and local lookup acceptance are not complete AES128 recovery. Distinctness99.991% and Section3 distinguisher experiments describe different events. Existing single-value-table lost-candidate conflict remains unchanged; not a new full-paper audit.

components.description: PDF13 Eq.(7),PDF14 Section4.2: the correct key satisfies the mixture zero-sum equation with probability1, including equivalent-key transport when finalMC is present. This is a relation, not successful singleton lookup or unique complete-key recovery.

PDF14: with only four texts, a guessed four-byte last key and four-byte previous key passes the four-byte zero-sum test with source probability2^-32. This does not give the six-text endpoint aggregate success.

limitations: Table 2 separates online work from reusable precomputation. The key output is AES-128; no AES-192/256 full-master-key budget is inferred.
Algorithm 2 explicitly checks residual key candidates; the source estimates average per-byte solutions but does not quantify worst-case completion.

Direct filtering retains candidate sets; complete master-key verification is additional work. No inference of AES-192/256 full master-key recovery is made. A source average of one solution is not a uniqueness guarantee on true-generated quartets.

field_conflicts.label: Singleton lookup loses valid key candidates
field_conflicts.description: The published singleton table overwrites multiple Eq.8 solutions. Source-reported online time does not bound a corrected set-valued lookup plus full-key completion. Own finite control demonstrates an actual standard AES-128 three-round input rectangle, not just an arbitrary quartet.

observations.reported: A[quartet] is assigned each matching key byte in ascending order, and only one byte is read back.

observations.locator: PDF p.13 Eq.8; independent finite substitution into the defining equation
observations.reported: AES-128 zero master key; plaintext first-column coordinates (0,0),(1,12),(0,12),(1,0); byte2 ciphertext quartet [93,248,238,98] admits key bytes52 and62, whereas the true third-round byte is52 and A retains62.
